bio_en: Artush Kocharyan of Bashgarni was a bold ARF haiduk from 1904, when he crossed into Ottoman Armenia with commander Mihran's band and fought at the Armenian village of Mosun. When the band was surrounded and disarmed by Russian Cossacks at Zor, he alone refused, breaking out with four comrades. Imprisoned twice by the tsarist government after the 1905 clashes, he joined the volunteers in the World War and was wounded in the battle of Revanduz in which Keri was killed. Jailed in Yerevan during the February 1921 uprising and condemned by the Cheka, he survived, but was murdered on the night of 24 February 1924, reportedly on the Cheka's orders.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: high. Nephew of Ghazar Kocharyan of Bashgarni (#23).
